sections.html:
Pike County had 18,889 residents at the 2020 census and an estimated 20,932 in July 2025, up from 17,869 in 2010. Zebulon is the county seat, and the tax commissioner keeps an office there at 79 Jackson Street.

Housing is mostly owner-occupied: 84.6% of homes are lived in by their owners. A typical owned home has a value of $305,600, rent runs about $993 a month, and a typical household takes in $86,719. The county has 7,737 housing units, and 106 building permits were issued in 2025. Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $1,869 a month in housing costs, and owners without one pay $605. The average commute is 35.7 minutes, so buyers are mostly working households who drive out of the county each day.

Buyers at these prices expect a well kept house. A listing with an open tax lien or half-finished repairs gives them a reason to wait or to ask for a lower price.

sections.h2: Which Pike County office should I call?
sections.html:
Call the tax commissioner about a bill and the assessors about a value. The two phone numbers differ by one digit, so it is easy to dial the wrong one.

  • Tax commissioner: (770) 567-2001, weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00. Online payments run through pikecountypay.com.
  • Tax assessors: (770) 567-2002 for returns, homestead forms, valuation and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: deed room at the county courthouse, and the place where a tax lien is recorded.
  • City of Zebulon: Pike County bills city property tax on the city's behalf, so there is no second counter for city residents.

Bills are addressed to the owner. A lender holding an escrow account will not receive one, so pass your copy along to the servicer.

Real estate and business personal property bills fall due December 1. A mobile home bill is due April 1. A United States Postal Service postmark counts as the payment date, and a metered mark does not.

Pike County bill types and late charges
Bill typeDue dateLate charge
Real estate and business personal propertyDecember 1Monthly interest, then 5% at 120 days, capped at 20%
Mobile homeApril 110% starting April 2

The county applies its penalty schedule in four steps:

  1. Interest posts on the 2nd of every month at prime plus 3%, divided by 12.
  2. A 5% penalty is added at 120 days, then again every 120 days, capped at 20%.
  3. Thirty days past the delinquent notice date, a FIFA is filed in the Clerk of Courts office.
  4. The account then moves to a contractor, and fees of $215 plus can be added for certified mail and a title search before the sale.

In the weeks before an auction the parcel is posted, photographed and advertised in the local paper for four weeks. Paying before the sale stage avoids every one of those costs.

Write to the assessors within 45 days of the notice date. An appeal sent after that cutoff cannot be accepted, so mail it early and keep a copy.

Argue one of three things: the property is not taxable, the value is wrong, or the value is out of line with similar parcels. A complaint that the tax amount is too high will not work, because the millage rate is a separate decision made by the county commissioners and the school board.

If the assessors stand by their number, a hearing before the Board of Equalization follows, or arbitration if you prefer. Superior Court is the last stop. Mobile home owners follow a shorter chain: 45 days with the assessors, then 21 days to reach the Board of Equalization.

Bring sale prices of similar nearby houses and photos of any defects. Those carry more weight than a general feeling that the value is high.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and other tax breaks
sections.html:
A homestead exemption is the first thing to check. You need to own and occupy the house on January 1, and the assessors must receive your form before April 1.

  • The assessors ask first-time filers to show their deed.
  • Pike adds its own county exemption amounts, and the bigger of the local and state figures applies.
  • Age 62 opens an extra exemption.
  • Working farmland may be taxed on 30% of market value, and conservation land on its use value. Both need a covenant of at least a decade.
  • Manufacturers can seek the freeport exemption in the January 1 to April 1 window.

The exemption continues from year to year until the home, its owner or the kind of exemption changes.

sections.h2: How is a Pike County bill built?
sections.html:
Taxable value is 40% of market value as of January 1, less exemptions. Rates come from the county commissioners and the school board separately. Each mill levies $1 on $1,000 of taxable value.

A real estate return is needed only after a purchase or an improvement, and it is filed January 1 through April 1. A required return that never gets filed draws a 10% charge on whatever value was left off. Equipment and other personal property goes on a fresh return every year.

sections.h2: What to have ready before you call
sections.html:
A short prep list saves a second phone call. Have your bill number or parcel number in hand, and know which year you are asking about. The commissioner's office is open weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00, and the assessors answer on their own line.

  • Your deed, if this is the first time you are filing a homestead form.
  • Your latest assessment notice, so you know the 45 day appeal window and its start date.
  • The name of your closing attorney or title company, who will request the written payoff.
  • Your mortgage servicer's contact, if the lender pays your tax from escrow.

Once you have the payoff in writing, compare it with the contract. If the buyer agreed to take on the current year's bill, make sure the settlement statement says so. If a FIFA was filed, ask what documents the office wants before it will release the lien, and ask how long the release takes after you pay.

Collect a written payoff and have the closing attorney deduct it at the table. Interest keeps growing monthly, so the number changes with the calendar.

  1. Phone (770) 567-2001 for the amount owed and any penalty.
  2. Ask whether a FIFA exists and what clears it.
  3. If the account is at the contractor stage, request the extra fees as a separate line.
  4. Check which year's bill falls on you under the contract.

Closing before the tax sale stage avoids newspaper and levy costs. A cash sale skips the repair list, the lender's appraisal and the wait for loan approval, so the closing date can fit around an inherited deed or unfinished work. The payoff is still taken from your proceeds at the table, the same way a mortgage payoff is.

faqs.q: When are Pike County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 1 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile home tax is due April 1.

faqs.q: How fast does Pike County add penalties?
faqs.a: Interest posts monthly, the first 5% penalty comes at 120 days, and the cap is 20%. Mobile homes get 10% on April 2.

faqs.q: Which Pike County office takes a homestead form?
faqs.a: The tax assessors, and it must be in hand before April 1. First-time homeowners should carry the deed.

faqs.q: Will a recorded FIFA stop a Pike County sale?
faqs.a: No. It is a lien that gets paid out of the proceeds. Ask the tax commissioner at (770) 567-2001 what the payoff is.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about my Pike County value?
faqs.a: The assessors at (770) 567-2002. Billing and payment go to the commissioner at (770) 567-2001.
